{{Citation}}
[[File:Astromechs_TotG.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An R5 unit, R4 unit and R7 unit]]
{{Quote|Hmmm... An R-series. No, no, not for a long time...|[[Gha Nachkt/Legends|Gha Nachkt]] to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] on having an R2 unit in stock|<ref name="Downfall">{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}</ref>}}
The '''R-series''' was an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] line created by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]], consisting of ten models&mdash;the [[P2-series astromech droid|P2-series]] and the [[R1-series astromech droid/Legends|R1]] through [[R9-series astromech droid|R9-series]] droids.

The R-series set several standards and paradigms that other astromech [[Droid/Legends|droids]] would later adhere to, such as fitting into a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] socket and having immense aftermarket upgrade and modification abilities. They were very common throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and by far the most famous and popular astromech droid series.

==Variations==
The R-series originally began with the [[P2-series astromech droid]], which was sold exclusively to the [[Old Republic shipping fleet]].

[[File:ThreeArtoos-SWCTP.png|thumb|left|300px|R2-series astromechs were a popular line of R-series droids.]]
The original [[R1-series astromech droid/Legends|R1 unit]] was designed from the body shell of the earlier [[Mark II reactor drone/Legends|Mark II reactor drone]] and was generally seen as an improvement of the P2 in its early years. The R1 was much less bulky than the P2, although still large, and able to hold 500 [[Starship/Legends|starship]] configurations. It was the first of the series to hold [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] navigational capabilities.

The [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 unit]] then far surpassed the R1. It was smaller, able to fit into a standard [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], and had more capabilities than its previous model. It was extremely popular with [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and was often used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. It could hold 700 configurations and featured full-spectrum, electromagnetic, heat, motion, and life-form sensors. The R2 unit was built for all environments, and came with an array of tools, which could include electric zappers, fuel-squirting compartments, pincers, lights, holoprojectors and computer arms able to access any computer. [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] is the most notable one of its class.

The [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3 unit]] was based on the R2's basic design, and was only distinguished visually by its clear dome. Unlike the R2, this unit was built for military and government uses, and could hold an immense amount of data.

The [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4 unit]] was designed for [[Antigrav/Legends|antigrav]] vehicles, and was more suitable to the public than its predecessor. Several of the R2's advantages were removed to lower the price, and make it more available.

[[File:DSquadAstromechs-FFp58.png|thumb|right|300px|Various models of R-series astromechs, including an R5 and R4 unit.]]
The [[R5-series astromech droid|R5 unit]] followed the R4 in many ways, including its inexpensive build. It was prone to malfunction and an unpleasant personality, so production ended quickly.

The [[R6-series astromech droid|R6 unit]] was released after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] to cover the huge failure of the R5 unit. Its programming was similar to that of the R2 unit, although it had a shell similar to that of the R5. The R6 boasted more storage than the R2, and was equipped with extra tools.

The [[R7-series astromech droid|R7]] model was designed specially for the [[E-7 E-wing multi-role starfighter|E-wing escort starfighter]], and did not show the same performance with other ships. Its systems were even more advanced than those of the R6 and R2 models.

The [[R8-series astromech droid|R8]] model was designed similarly to the R7, but with a satellite dish instead of a sensor "eye." It was built to accommodate a larger array of starfighters, instead of focusing on a particular ship, such as the E-wing.

The [[R9-series astromech droid|R9]] model was similar to the R2, but with enhanced systems.
